scenes.heading: Transactions
scenes.narration: Delta transactions guarantee that a write either fully succeeds or has no effect, which is what makes operations like MERGE safe.

scenes.heading: The ACID guarantees
scenes.narration: Atomicity means a commit applies completely or not at all, so there are no half-written tables. Consistency keeps schema and constraints intact through every change. Isolation shields readers from in-flight writes, and durability ensures committed data survives failures.

scenes.heading: An upsert with MERGE
scenes.code:
MERGE INTO sales_data AS t
USING df_updates AS s
ON t.order_id = s.order_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;
scenes.narration: This MERGE matches incoming rows against the target table on order id. Rows that already exist are updated, while new rows are inserted, all in one statement. Delta wraps the entire operation in a single transaction, so either every change lands or none do.

scenes.text: Because MERGE is transactional, concurrent readers never see a partially applied upsert, keeping your table trustworthy.
scenes.narration: Because MERGE runs as one transaction, concurrent readers never see a partially applied upsert, which keeps the table trustworthy.
